title: Kwek-kwek
intro: Crispy orange-battered quail eggs with a dipping sauce.
ingredients: ½ cup water, plus as needed
½ tsp annatto powder or orange food coloring (optional)
steps: Peel the boiled quail eggs and pat them dry.
Whisk flour, water, egg, annatto, salt, and pepper into a smooth, thick batter.
Coat each egg in a little flour, then dip it in the batter.
Fry in hot oil in small batches until the coating is crisp and cooked through.
Drain on a rack or paper towel and serve with your preferred dipping sauce.

title: Tortang talong
intro: Smoky eggplant wrapped in a tender egg coating.
steps: Grill or boil eggplants until tender. Cool, peel, and flatten gently while keeping the stem attached.
Beat eggs with salt and pepper in a shallow bowl.
Dip the flattened eggplant into the beaten egg, coating both sides.
Pan-fry in oil over medium heat until golden on both sides and the egg is fully set.
Serve hot with rice and a dipping sauce if desired.

title: Tortang giniling
intro: A filling Filipino omelet with seasoned ground meat.
steps: Heat a little oil and sauté onion and tomato until softened.
Add ground meat; cook, breaking it apart, until no pink remains and it is thoroughly cooked. Let it cool slightly.
Beat eggs with salt and pepper, then mix in the cooked meat.
Heat remaining oil in a pan. Pour in the mixture in small portions or one omelet.
Cook over medium-low heat until set, then flip carefully and cook the other side through.

title: Itlog na may kamatis
steps: Beat eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a pan; sauté garlic briefly if using.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft and juicy.
Pour in eggs and gently stir until softly set and fully cooked.
Serve immediately with rice.

title: Nilagang itlog
intro: A simple kitchen staple for meals, snacks, or baon.
steps: Place eggs in a saucepan and cover with water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer gently. Cook about 9–12 minutes for firm yolks, adjusting for egg size and preference.
Transfer eggs to cold water until cool enough to handle.
Peel and serve, or refrigerate promptly if saving for later.
